answer: Solar calculators size and price a home system from what you use: panels from your daily units and your city's sun, an inverter from the load, a battery from the backup you want, and the bill saving under net billing. Start from your units or your appliance list; every result shows the formula and the city data behind it.

sections.h2: Where to start: size the system
p: If you know your units, the [[D7|solar system size calculator]] or the [[N17|solar size from your bill]], month by month, gives the kW of panels. If you know your appliances, the [[D8|five marla house]], [[D12|ten marla house]] and [[D13|one kanal house]] calculators and the one for a [[N13|mosque or shop]] size the panels, inverter and battery together.

For one part at a time: the [[D2|solar panel wattage calculator]] for the panels, the [[D4|inverter size calculator]] for the inverter, the [[D1|solar battery size calculator]] for the battery and the [[D16|charge controller size calculator]] for an off-grid controller. A home with no grid at all needs the [[D3|off-grid solar calculator]], which also checks the weakest month. For single loads, see [[D5|how many panels run an AC]], the [[D15|tubewell solar calculator]] and the [[D6|solar panel for a twelve-volt battery]].

Prices come from dated dealer and installer lists: the [[D9|solar panel price]] per watt and per panel, the [[D14|solar system price]] for whole systems, and the [[N3|solar quote checker]] to test a quote against them. New grid connections are on net billing: the [[D10|net billing calculator]] shows the bill with solar, and the [[D11|net billing guide]] explains the rules.

The [[N6|solar forecast for tomorrow]] estimates the next day's output for your city, the [[N12|cleaning loss calculator]] shows what dust is costing, and the [[N14|battery autonomy calculator]] how many cloudy days the battery covers.

faq.q: What size solar system do I need?
faq.a: Divide the units you use a day by the units one kW of panels makes a day in your city, then round up to whole panels. The [[D7|solar system size calculator]] does it with the sun data for Pakistani cities.

faq.q: How much does a solar system cost in Pakistan?
faq.a: It depends on the size, and larger systems cost less per watt. The [[D14|solar system price]] page gives dated ranges for common sizes, and the [[solar-price-tracker|solar price tracker]] shows how they have moved.

Not for new connections, which are on net billing: imports are billed at the slab rate and exports bought at a flat buyback rate far below it. Agreements signed before {{data.tariff.net_billing.existing_cutoff}} keep the old terms until they expire.

On-grid has the shorter payback where the supply is reliable; hybrid adds a battery for loadshedding at a higher price. The [[H1|Home Power Planner]] compares both, and backup without solar, for your own home.
